scenes.title: Never a stranger at the Club again
scenes.say: This is the Club des Affaires of the Foire du Valais: about fifty business leaders who meet four or five times a year. They come, but many don't know each other. I built a platform so that nobody is ever a stranger at the Club again.

scenes.title: No member name in public
scenes.say: From the outside, the showcase never shows a single member name. Anyone curious can request an invitation, with or without a sponsor.

scenes.title: A two-minute request
scenes.say: Anna fills in a two-minute form. No account is created yet: the team stays in control of who joins.

scenes.title: Request sent
scenes.say: Her request is on its way.

scenes.title: An admin that explains itself
scenes.say: On the team's side, the administration opens with a short guide. The events team has very little time, so six simple gestures are enough, and everything else is computed.

scenes.title: Accept a member in one click
scenes.say: Here is Anna's request. One click accepts it and creates her account. A welcome e-mail with a personal sign-in link is prepared for her.

scenes.title: Camille's home
scenes.say: Meet Camille, who joined the Club this year. Her home shows her album of the members she has met, and the Club's progress: fourteen percent of the member pairs already know each other. At twenty percent, the whole Club wins a round of Petite Arvine.

scenes.title: The album of member cards
scenes.say: The album shows every member's card: their sector, their passions, what they love and what they hate, what they can help with, and what they are looking for. Camille needs help with the Swiss German market.

scenes.title: Lukas can help
scenes.say: Lukas, a pillar of the Club from Brig, can help with exactly that. His contact details are still locked: they only unlock after a real meeting.

scenes.title: The autumn dinner
scenes.say: Camille is coming to the autumn dinner. Each evening has its own icebreaker: a people bingo during the standing drinks, then rotating tables at dinner.

scenes.title: Three introductions, and why
scenes.say: Before the dinner, the platform introduces her to three people, and explains why. With Lukas, they share a love of Petite Arvine and ski touring, and they can help each other: digital for him, the Swiss German market for her.

scenes.title: She scans his badge
scenes.say: At the dinner, she scans the QR code on his badge. The app even tells her which square of her bingo he can tick.

scenes.title: Contacts unlock after a real meeting
scenes.say: One tap, and his card joins her album. His phone, his LinkedIn and a vCard for her address book are now unlocked. No cold messages, ever.

scenes.title: A bingo computed for each guest
scenes.say: Her bingo grid is computed for her alone, from the people present tonight, and a full card is always possible. A full line means a glass at the bar.

scenes.title: The whole Club gets closer
scenes.say: Every real encounter moves the whole Club closer to its next milestone.

scenes.title: French, German, English
scenes.say: And everything works in French, German and English, including the events.

scenes.title: The dashboard
scenes.say: Back to the team. The dashboard shows the encounters of the year, the new members, the members who are still isolated, and the invitation requests to handle.

scenes.title: Prepare the dinner
scenes.say: A week before the dinner, the team clicks Prepare.

scenes.title: Rotating tables in one click
scenes.say: One click generates the rotating tables: thirty-eight guests, three courses, about two hundred and fifty new pairs, and a single repeat.

scenes.title: Badges with QR codes
scenes.say: Another click prints the name badges, each with its own QR code.

scenes.title: It works today
scenes.say: It runs today, secure by default and covered by four hundred automated tests, for about thirty francs a month. A club that knows itself comes back together.
